# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.

# Intake brief — Test execution policy: tests are only ever run through the test skill

**Headline:** Establish an explicit, universally-installed agent policy that test
commands are never invoked directly — all agent-initiated test execution goes
through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`) — backed by a
deterministic conformance test, with no exceptions.

## Problem statement

Agents sometimes run tests with ad-hoc commands (`pytest …`, `npm test`,
`npx vitest run`, `node --test …`). Such runs are invisible to the per-repo
test cache that the test skill populates (keyed by git state + scope, 2h TTL),
so the audit skill cannot auto-verify execution-dependent ACs from them — the
guarantee "green means the canonical runner verified it, and the audit can
prove it" only holds when execution goes through the test skill. The current
guidance is scattered and per-skill ("before `in_review`, run via `/skill:test`"),
not an absolute, no-exceptions policy, and several skill docs still instruct
direct test invocation.

## Users

- **AI implement/refactor/triage/review agents** — must never bypass the
  canonical cached runner; when they need to reproduce or verify, they route
  through the test skill.
- **Producers / reviewers** — rely on a green run meaning "executed by the
  test-skill runner, cached, audit-verifiable", not an ad-hoc command.
- **Audit skill** — auto-verifies execution-dependent ACs from cached
  test-skill runs (read-only `query_cached()`); ad-hoc runs are invisible and
  degrade verification to auto-execute (F3) or partial.

Example user stories:

- As an implement agent, I want the policy to forbid direct test commands so a
  green gate always means the canonical runner executed and cached the suite.
- As a producer, I want a single, no-exceptions rule installed globally so no
  skill or session encourages ad-hoc test invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (policy)** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (and thus the globally installed
  `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) contains an explicit **Test execution policy**:
  agents must never invoke test commands directly (ad-hoc `pytest`, `npm test`,
  `vitest`, `node --test`, etc.); every agent-initiated test run goes through
  the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`), covering full/changed scope
  and unit/smoke types — with no exceptions.
  *Verification:* the policy section is present and the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` reflects it (symlinked install).
- **AC2 (skills reworded)** Every agent-facing directive in
  `skill/*/SKILL.md` that instructs running tests directly is reworded to route
  through the test skill — at minimum `skill/triage/SKILL.md` ("Prefer quiet
  test commands…"), `skill/report/SKILL.md` ("Run with `python3 -m pytest
  ./tests`") and `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` ("`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`")
  — and `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`'s "quiet pytest contract" phrasing is
  clarified. `<skill> ## Tests` sections are reworded, not deleted.
  *Verification:* `rg` across `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, `skill/*/SKILL.md`,
  `command/` shows no remaining agent-facing direct test-command directive.
- **AC3 (conformance test)** A deterministic conformance test (following the
  existing `tests/test_*_skill_doc.py` pattern, e.g.
  `tests/test_test_skill_directory.py` or an extension of
  `tests/test_test_skill_doc.py`) scans agent-facing skill/command/global docs
  for prohibited direct test-command patterns and fails on any miss; the only
  allowed matches are legitimate infrastructure references (the test skill's
  own runner docs, git hooks/CI, the audit F2 suite-command resolution doc) and
  the single known snippet tracked by SA-0MSN6FBFF009VCOB (whitelisted with a
  comment referencing that item).
  *Verification:* the new test fails when a prohibited directive is introduced
  and passes at HEAD.
- **AC4 (docs)** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (notably `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and the test skill's `SKILL.md`).
- **AC5 (full suite)** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Documentation-only (producer decision Q1=a).** No pi extension, no
  `user_bash`/`tool_call` interception guard, no runtime block of direct test
  commands. Enforcement is policy + conformance test, not a technical guard.
- **Universal (producer decision Q2=a).** The policy lives in the canonical
  `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and skill docs, installed globally, so it applies to all
  agent sessions, not just this repository's sessions.
- **No exceptions (producer decision Q3=no).** No sanctioned ad-hoc direct test
  invocation for agents. Automated pipelines that already route through the
  test-skill runner are not agent-invoked ad-hoc runs and are out of scope:
  the pre-push hook (`--scope full`), `implement.py finish` (delegates to
  `guarded_run_all`), and the audit F3 auto-execution.
- **Do not duplicate SA-0MSN6FBFF009VCOB** (open: fix the
  `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` direct `npm test` snippet). That file's
  snippet is fixed by that item; this item whitelists it in the conformance
  test (with a traceable comment) rather than editing the same lines.
- **Keep the test skill's own internal runner docs intact.** The audit F2
  suite-command resolution prose (`.pi/test-config.json`, `npm --silent test`,
  pytest conventions) documents how the canonical runner resolves commands — it
  is infrastructure documentation, not a directive to run tests directly.
- **Surgical edits.** Only reword the direct-invocation directives; do not
  rewrite unrelated skill prose.

## Existing state

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (installed globally as `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` via
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`) requires `/skill:test` before `in_review`
  ("Test-failure triage policy"), and `skill/implement/SKILL.md` §finish
  already delegates the gate to the test skill's `guarded_run_all` — so the
  *gate* paths are canonical. What is missing is an absolute, no-exceptions
  policy statement + a conformance test, and several skills still contain
  direct-invocation instructions (see AC2).
- Confirmed direct-invocation instructions at HEAD: `skill/triage/SKILL.md`
  line ~58 ("Prefer quiet test commands (`pytest -q` / `npm --silent test`)"),
  `skill/report/SKILL.md` line ~280 ("Run with `python3 -m pytest ./tests`"),
  `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` line ~142 ("`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`"),
  `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` line ~84 ("following the quiet pytest contract").
- `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` line ~89 documents that agents
  "run `npm --silent test` directly, which bypasses the per-repo test cache" —
  already tracked by the open item SA-0MSN6FBFF009VCOB.
- Existing doc-conformance tests to model the new test on:
  `tests/test_audit_skill_doc.py`, `tests/test_cleanup_skill_doc.py`,
  `tests/test_test_skill_doc.py`, `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py`,
  `tests/test_command_doc_hygiene.py`.

## Desired change

1. Add a **Test execution policy** section to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` stating the
   absolute rule (never run tests directly; always `/skill:test`; no
   exceptions), and install it globally.
2. Reword the remaining direct-invocation directives in `triage`, `report`,
   `pane-triage` and `refactor` skills to route through the test skill.
3. Add a deterministic doc-conformance test enforcing the policy.
4. Update related docs (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, test skill docs).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — Add the universal Test execution policy section.
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — Reword "Prefer quiet test commands…" to route local reproduction through the test skill.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — Reword "Run with `python3 -m pytest ./tests`" to test-skill invocation.
- `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — Reword the `## Tests` section's `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` to the test skill.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — Clarify "quiet pytest contract" phrasing to reference the test skill's output contract.
- `tests/test_test_skill_doc.py` (or a new `tests/test_test_skill_directory.py`) — Add the policy-conformance scan with an explicit whitelist.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — Document the policy and the conformance test.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — No functional change expected (already installs `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); verify the symlink reflects the new section.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: conformance-test false positives.** A grep over skill/command docs may
  match test-file imports or legitimate infrastructure prose (e.g. the audit F2
  suite-command doc, the pre-push hook docs). Mitigation: scope the regex to
  agent-facing directive patterns and maintain an explicit, commented
  whitelist.
- **Risk: scope creep.** The item is documentation-only by decision; adjacent
  ideas (a blocking `user_bash` extension, runtime guard, folding in unrelated
  doc rewrites) are explicitly out of scope and must not be pulled in. Recorded
  as the umbrella enforcement item; any future technical guard would be a
  separate work item.
- **Risk: duplicating SA-0MSN6FBFF009VCOB.** Editing the
  `resolve-pr-comments` snippet here would duplicate the open item's planned
  work. Mitigation: whitelist with a traceable coordination comment instead of
  editing.
- **Assumption:** automated gates (pre-push hook, `implement.py finish` via
  `guarded_run_all`, audit F3 auto-execution) already route through the
  test-skill runner and are outside this policy's scope — they are pipeline
  infrastructure, not agent-invoked ad-hoc runs.
- **Assumption:** `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlinked install of
  `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, so one source file is edited; verify after install via
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` if the symlink is stale.
- **Assumption:** rewording `<skill> ## Tests` sections to route through the
  test skill preserves the intent (how to verify that skill) while removing
  the direct-invocation instruction.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSN6FBFF009VCOB** (open, `plan_complete`) — "resolve-pr-comments:
  replace direct npm test snippet with test skill invocation". Single-known-snippet
  fix; this item whitelists it (with a traceable comment) instead of editing the
  same lines.
- **SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY** (completed) — cache full test-suite results for reuse
  across ship/audit/implement workflows; the cache contract this policy protects.
- **SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q** (completed) — live-repo guard-ownership parity:
  `implement.py`'s test runs now delegate to the test skill's `guarded_run_all`.
- **SA-0MSAC1IAS007I3K8** — follow-up wiring item documented in the test skill
  (referenced, not duplicated).
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP / SA-0MSTN8CWM003AAU9** — audit F3 auto-execution and
  F4 never-block; the cache contract this policy protects.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the enforcement be (a) documentation-only — strengthening policy across all skills to mandate the test skill, (b) technical enforcement — a Pi extension (`user_bash` hook) intercepting/blocking direct test commands, or (c) both?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **a** — documentation-only. Source: interactive reply in intake session.
- Q2: "Should this apply to (a) all agent sessions universally, or (b) only the SorraAgents repository and its agent skills?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **a** — universal (via the globally installed AGENTS_GLOBAL.md / skills). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Are there any legitimate exceptions where direct test invocation is allowed (CI runs, pre-push git hooks, operator debugging)?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **no** — no exceptions. Interpretation: automated gates (pre-push hook, implement finish via `guarded_run_all`, audit F3) already route through the canonical test-skill runner and are not agent-invoked ad-hoc runs, so they are out of scope, not exceptions. Source: interactive reply.

# Standup skill should commit and push generated standup files

## Problem Statement

`generate_standup.py` writes its daily report to `./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md` but
leaves the file unversioned: the operator must manually commit and push it, and
the file lingers as an untracked artifact (currently masked only by a machine-local
`.git/info/exclude` stopgap). The skill should persist its own output — commit and
push the report file it just wrote — so standup history is versioned automatically.

## Users

- **Operator running the standup skill** — wants standup history tracked in git and
  pushed without manual steps.

### User Stories

- As an operator, I want `generate_standup.py` to commit and push the report file it
  writes so standup history is versioned without manual git steps.
- As an operator, I want a deterministic/offline escape hatch so scripted and test
  runs never touch git.
- As an operator, I want commit/push failures (offline, no git, no upstream, bad
  author identity) to be warnings, not errors — the local report must still be written.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After `generate_standup.py` writes a report file (default dated path under
   `standups/` **or** an explicit `--output-path`), it commits **only that file**
   with a clear commit message and pushes the current branch, when run inside a git
   repository. (Tested with a hermetic real-git sandbox.)
2. When the current branch is `main`, the script still commits locally but **does
   not push**, logging a warning — honouring the repo policy "push only to dev,
   never to main" (AGENTS.md).
3. A new `--no-commit` flag disables all git operations (mirroring `--no-sync`);
   `--json` to stdout (no file written) performs no commit/push. Re-running when the
   file is unchanged is an idempotent no-op, not an error.
4. All commit/push failures — non-git directory, unborn/empty repo, missing upstream,
   unset author identity, offline push — are **non-fatal**: the report is still
   generated and written, a warning is logged to stderr, and the exit code is
   unchanged.
5. `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the commit-and-push default, `--no-commit`,
   and the `main` push guard; the machine-local `standups/` entry in
   `.git/info/exclude` is removed.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; new tests cover commit+push,
   the `main` guard, `--no-commit`, idempotence and non-fatal failures.

## Constraints

- **Surgical commits only** — never `git add -A` / `git add .`; exactly the file
  written by this run.
- Failure handling mirrors the existing sync-first pattern
  (`worklog_sync.py`): non-fatal, warning to stderr, exit code unchanged.
- New flag name must mirror the existing convention: `--no-commit` beside
  `--no-sync`; default is commit+push **on**.
- Push targets the current branch's upstream; never force-push; never push `main`.
- Author identity comes from the repo/build host git config (no knowledge of
  credentials in the script); author-gate failure is non-fatal.
- No change to report content/format or output-path resolution (out of scope;
  touched only to route the commit).

## Existing State

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — writes the report (default
  `./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md` or `--output-path`), syncs the worklog first via the
  shared `worklog_sync.py` helper, `--no-sync` escape hatch. No git commit/push.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` — documents Invocation flags, sync-first, report structure.
- `.git/info/exclude` (machine-local, this checkout) — contains `standups/` stopgap
  added so the implement dirty-tree gate passes without touching generated files;
  comment references SA-0MTYJ4MGO007O22W. Once files are auto-committed the tree is
  clean immediately, so the stopgap is obsolete.
- Repo push policy: "Push only to `dev` — never to `main`" (AGENTS.md).
- Shared helpers available: `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` (non-fatal patterns),
  `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (hermetic real-git test factories), repo-root
  `live_repo_guard.py` (tests must not mutate their own checkout — a test using
  `git_sandbox` factories in `tmp_path` is required, not a live-repo commit).

## Desired Change

- Add a `commit_report_file(path, project_root, ...)` helper to
  `generate_standup.py`: `git add <path>` → `git commit -m "<message>"` →
  `git push`, all run with `cwd=project_root` (or an injectable runner for tests),
  every step non-fatal with a warning.
- Skip commit silently when the file has no changes ("nothing to commit").
- Skip push (with warning) when the current branch is `main`.
- Wire the helper into `main()` after the file-write branches (default path,
  `--output-path` markdown, `--output-path` JSON); no-op for `--json` to stdout.
- Add `--no-commit` flag parsed in `main()`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** committing history into the repo is a standing behaviour change to the skill; report *content* changes (e.g. project-title header, SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ) are recorded as separate work items, not this one.
- **Silent-blob risk:** if the local `standups/` exclusion is *not* removed, `git add` silently skips the file and the commit becomes a "nothing to commit" no-op — the operator gets no versioned file and no error. The exclusion removal (Key Files) must therefore land together with the script change; a fresh clone without the exclusion needs no action.
- **Push race:** `git push` is non-force and single-file; concurrent pushes from other agents may reject with non-fast-forward — non-fatal warning, report still written, operator retries later.
- **Local divergence when on `main`:** committing locally without pushing on `main` can leave a local-ahead state; accepted per policy (never push `main`), surfaced via the warning.
- **Author identity:** unset `user.name`/`user.email` on a host makes the commit fail — non-fatal, mirroring the author-gate handling already accepted for `wl sync`.
- **Assumption:** the report file always lives inside the project root's git working tree (default path and typical `--output-path`); a path outside the repo is a non-fatal failed commit/warning.
- **Assumption:** tests use the hermetic `git_sandbox` factories in `tmp_path` only — never the live repo checkout (live_repo_guard F4/F5).

## Key Files

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — new `--no-commit` flag, `commit_report_file()` helper, wiring after file writes.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` — document commit-and-push default, `--no-commit`, `main` guard.
- `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_commit.py` — new test module (uses `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` factories, `tmp_path` only — never the live checkout).
- `.git/info/exclude` — remove the local `standups/` entry (machine-local implementation step in the main checkout).

## Related Work

- **SA-0MTVB0NAQ007UKID** (completed, in_review) — Standup writes to
  `./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md` by default; this item builds on that output routing.
- **WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K** (completed) — sync-first + `--no-sync` escape hatch; the
  pattern this item mirrors for `--no-commit` and non-fatal handling.
- **SA-0MTOMCML900254CI** (completed) — `--worklog-dir` / `WL_WORKLOG_DIR`
  cwd-independence; commit must target the resolved project root, not cwd.
- **SA-0MTYJ4MGO007O22W** (completed) — refactoring epic that tracks the
  `.git/info/exclude` stopgap comment; exclusion removal resolves that debt.
- **SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ** (in-progress) — project title in standup header; related
  but independent (report content, not commit behaviour).
- **SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL / SA-0MUFNU2WM00049A9** (completed) — regression-detection
  fixes in the same script; relevant for full-suite regression safety.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should be committed in a run?" — Answer (operator): "Only the report file written in this run (e.g. today's `standups/2026_10_13.md`)" — surgical, single file. Source: interactive reply.

- Q: "Failure handling and escape hatch?" — Answer (operator): "Non-fatal warning + `--no-commit` flag to skip" — mirrors `--no-sync`, exit unchanged on failure. Source: interactive reply.

- Q: "Git exclusion and push target?" — Answer (operator): "Remove the local `standups/` exclusion, use plain `git add`+`commit`+`push` of the current branch, refusing to auto-push when on `main`." Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief — find-related: improve keyword relevance (IDF/title weighting)

## Problem statement

Keyword extraction in `find_related.py` is frequency-ranked and capped to the
top 8 (`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`), but raw frequency lets corpus-generic words
dominate, so `wl search` queries are built from terms that carry little signal
and the returned "related" items are often unrelated. Title terms and
distinctive domain terms are not weighted above generic body words.

## Users

- **Pi agents** running `/skill:find-related` during intake/plan/implement —
  they consume the "Related work (automated report)" section appended to work
  item descriptions and need genuinely related precedent.
- **Producers** reviewing work items — they spend time triaging spurious
  "related" links.

Example user stories:

- As a build agent, I want the related-work section for a find-related skill
  improvement to surface the skill's own prior reviews and keyword tests, so I
  don't re-read unrelated lint items.
- As a producer, I want to trust that at least the top-ranked related items
  are on-topic, so triage is fast.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9 ("Review find related skill"), at least 2 of the
      top 3 related work items are genuinely related to the find-related skill
      (manual reviewer judgement, documented in the work item).
- [ ] Keyword selection is deterministic across re-runs: identical input
      returns an identical keyword list (idempotency preserved; ties remain
      broken alphabetically).
- [ ] Distinctive domain terms outrank corpus-generic terms in the extracted
      keyword ordering (asserted by new unit tests; title tokens weight higher
      than body tokens; expanded project-generic stop-word list drops
      "work"/"item"/"report"/"review"/"skill" where they add no signal).
- [ ] Existing find-related unit tests pass or are updated only where they
      codify the old pure-frequency ordering; new tests assert the new ranking
      behaviour, including determinism and stop-word handling.
- [ ] No increase in runtime beyond the v3 bound: the per-keyword `wl search`
      subprocess count remains capped (≤ `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` ranking-heuristic tables,
      and README or wiki entries where relevant.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the v3 feedback-loop fix: the automated-report section is stripped
  from the description before extraction; no unbounded keyword growth.
- Conservative policy: prefer false negatives over false positives. A term is
  only a keyword if it adds genuine signal.
- `wl search` subprocess spawns are the dominant runtime cost (~0.4–0.5s each);
  keyword selection must stay within the existing capped fan-out. No new
  per-keyword subprocesses beyond the v3 cap. (True corpus-wide IDF via a
  dedicated per-term document-frequency pass would violate this cap.)
- Preserve report compactness (keyword lists per repo file capped at
  `MAX_KEYWORDS_PER_FILE`, `(+N more)` markers) and the deterministic
  tie-breaking (alphabetical) guarantee.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-boosting title terms** could let a generic title word (e.g. "review",
  "skill") dominate the keyword list and reproduce today's problem in a new
  form — mitigate by combining title boost *with* the project stop-word
  expansion, and assert in tests that a generic title word does not outrank a
  distinctive body term.
- **Aggressive stop-word expansion** can drop a genuinely distinguishing term
  (e.g. "report" distinguishing report-related skills). Conservative policy
  (prefer false negatives) accepts this; document any term added to
  `STOP_WORDS` in code comments with its rationale.
- **Regression risk in keyword tests**: `test_frequency_ordering_puts_descriptive_core_first`
  and several `test_find_related.py` keyword tests codify pure-frequency
  ordering; updates must preserve the deterministic/alphabetical-tie contract
  or they become flaky.
- **Scope creep**: sibling items SA-0MUG46YR2006URF4 (verbose keyword
  listing) and SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ (runtime <5s parallelisation) touch the
  same script but are separate work — do not fold them into this item;
  coordinate only to avoid merge conflicts in `find_related.py`.

## Assumptions

- The wl search `score` field (BM25/hybrid) continues to rank the *returned*
  items; this item changes keyword *selection* only, unless the implementer
  demonstrates a re-ranking need in review.
- True corpus-wide IDF is unavailable without extra subprocesses; the
  title-boost + stop-word-list approach is accepted as the "or equivalent"
  permitted by the seed context.

## Existing state

- `extract_keywords(title, description)` concatenates `title` + description
  and returns unique tokens ordered by **descending raw frequency** (ties
  alphabetical), after stop-word/length/numeric filtering
  (`find_related.py:177–216`).
- Title tokens are counted identically to body tokens (the title is just
  prepended to the combined text), so a title's single occurrence carries no
  more weight than one body occurrence.
- `STOP_WORDS` is a general English list only; project-generic terms
  ("work", "item", "report", "review", "skill", "related", "find") are not
  excluded.
- `search_and_dedup` queries the top-8 frequency keywords, one `wl search`
  each, and ranks *returned* items by the `score` field — but the candidate
  set is fixed by keyword *selection*, so retrieval quality is bounded by
  extraction quality.
- **Live reproduction (this intake session, SA-0MUG46NJE003JOCD):** a
  `find_related.py` run returned 3 unrelated completed lint work items
  (`SA-0MS3ATYK1003IGR7`, `SA-0MS3ATYU5009Q3J8`, `SA-0MS3ATZ490094SSI` — all
  "Do not catch blind exception (BLE001)" findings against `find_related.py`)
  and audit docs as top repo matches — matched on generic words
  ("acceptance", "audit", "behaviour"). The searched top-8 keywords were
  `related, skill, find, terms, keyword, audit, frequency, generic`.
- Existing test `test_frequency_ordering_puts_descriptive_core_first`
  (`tests/test_find_related_v3.py:107`) codifies pure frequency ordering
  (`keywords[:3] == ["search", "optimize", "speed"]`) and will need to be
  updated/renamed to assert the new weighting.

## Desired change

- **Weight keywords** so distinctive domain terms outrank corpus-generic
  terms, using inverse-document-frequency (IDF) or an equivalent
  zero-extra-cost proxy, and boost title terms over body/description terms.
  Deliverable is an *ordering* change to `extract_keywords` (still
  deterministic, still capped at `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` for search)
  — mechanism options for the implementer:
  1. **Static title boost + expanded project stop-word list** (deterministic,
     zero subprocess cost; recommended as the baseline): multiply/weight title
     tokens; add project-generic terms to `STOP_WORDS`.
  2. **Result-set-size IDF proxy**: use the `count`/result-set size returned by
     the *existing* 8 `wl search` spawns — a generic term returns ~20 (cap),
     a distinctive term returns few. Zero extra subprocesses, but only
     available *after* the first sweep, so it best augments ordering/display
     rather than selecting the sweep. (True corpus IDF via direct worklog DB /
     FTS reads is explicitly **out of scope** — it bypasses the `wl` CLI as
     source of truth and couples the script to the DB schema.)
- **Expand `STOP_WORDS`** with project-generic terms that add no signal.
- The seed's optional **minimum relevance threshold** is deferred:
  implementation may drop a keyword with no results, but the related-items
  list keeps its soft top-3 cap (`MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS`) — see Appendix Q2.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py` — `extract_keywords`,
  `STOP_WORDS`, keyword-ordering logic (`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` selection).
- `tests/test_find_related.py` — existing keyword unit tests
  (`test_keywords_from_title`, `test_keywords_excludes_common_stop_words`, …).
- `tests/test_find_related_v3.py` — `TestKeywordRankingAndNoise`,
  `TestExtractKeywordsSkipsReportSection`.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — keyword-extraction description, ranking
  heuristics tables, `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` docs.

## Related work

### Potentially related work items

- **SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9** — "Review find related skill" (completed). The v3
  review that discovered this item; the acceptance basis for AC1.
- **SA-0MUG46YR2006URF4** — "find-related: verbose output lists all extracted
  keywords, not the searched subset" (open, same discovery). Sibling issue on
  `find_related.py` (diagnostics, not ranking). If both are implemented, the
  verbose line should reflect the *searched* subset.
- **SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ** — "find-related: bring runtime back under the 5s
  target" (open, same discovery). Parallelises the 8 `wl search` calls;
  overlaps the runtime constraint — any keyword-selection change should stay
  agnostic to (and compatible with) that parallelisation.
- **SA-0MQ8MW73R001NSQZ** — "Unit tests for keyword extraction" (completed).
  Existing keyword-extraction coverage.
- **SA-0MQ8MWVXH004F63S** — "Worklog search and deduplication logic"
  (completed). `search_and_dedup`/ranking history.
- **SA-0MRPL5WLZ000JZ9V** — "Related Items is too broad" (completed). Prior
  relevance/compactness work on the same report; both items cap repo-file
  keyword lists, soft top-3 limits.

### Potentially related docs

- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — `### Ranking heuristics`, `### Configurable
  limits`, keywords decision-logic step 2.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — find-related report usage in intake.

### Automated related-work report

A `find_related.py` run on this item during intake (2026-10) inserted a
"Related work (automated report)" section showing the current bug in action
(3 unrelated BLE001 lint items + audit docs); regenerated report should be
re-evaluated after this change as manual verification of AC1.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should 'IDF or equivalent' be implemented given the subprocess cap
  (true corpus wide document-frequency requires a per-term pass)?" — **OPEN
  QUESTION.** Recommended (deferred to developer under Constraints): static
  title boost + expanded project stop-word list, with the result-set-size
  proxy as an optional augmentation from the existing 8 spawns; a direct
  worklog DB/FTS read for true IDF is out of scope (bypasses `wl` CLI,
  couples to DB schema). Source: seed context ("or equivalent",
  "subprocess count remains capped") + code inspection of
  `extract_keywords`/`search_and_dedup` (title currently counted once like any
  body token).
- Q2: "Should a minimum relevance threshold be enforced (dropping weak items,
  potentially yielding an empty related list)?" — **OPEN QUESTION.**
  Recommended: defer; keep the soft top-3 cap (`MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS`), drop
  only keywords with no results. Rationale: conservative policy prefers false
  negatives, but an always-empty report would break producer expectations
  built on the soft-cap behaviour. Source: seed context ("Optionally require
  a minimum relevance threshold") + existing `MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS` soft-cap
  comment in `find_related.py`.
- Note: interactive interview skipped — seed context supplied problem,
  evidence, proposed improvement, ACs, and constraints; remaining choices are
  implementation-detail options recorded above for the producer to override
  at review.

# Soft-deleted work items can be resurrected by status updates and re-dispatched

## Problem statement

A soft-deleted work item (one where `wl delete` has set `deletedBy`) can be resurrected via a status update, after which the downtime dispatcher re-selects it for dispatch. This caused the false-positive test-failure item SA-0MUJ14FQQ006R3PD to be worked twice after it had already been deleted.

## Users

- **Agent automation (Map, Build, etc.)**: agents rely on the downtime dispatcher to assign work and on soft-delete to permanently exclude items. Resurrection breaks this contract and wastes capacity.
- **Operator/Producer**: expects that a deleted work item will never re-appear in the dispatch queue or be worked by an agent.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **`wl update --status` refuses to change the status of a soft-deleted item.** The command checks `deletedBy` before accepting any status mutation and returns a clear error.
2. **`StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed` refuses to claim a soft-deleted item.** When `wl show` returns a non-empty `deletedBy`, `ensure_claimed` raises a `ClaimError` (or equivalent) instead of silently issuing a `wl update --status in-progress`. `require_claimed` also checks `deletedBy` in addition to status.
3. **The downtime dispatcher excludes soft-deleted items.** The worker filters out items where `deletedBy` is set (in addition to existing `status`-based filters) at the candidate-selection stage, before the Herdr list is consumed.
4. **All three guards are covered by automated tests.** Unit tests verify each refusal path; integration tests verify the dispatcher does not dispatch a soft-deleted item.

## Constraints

- The fix must be backward compatible: items already in flight at the time of the fix must not be affected.
- The `wl delete` command already sets `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; this fix ensures those fields are respected everywhere they matter.
- Performance impact must be negligible — each guard is a single-field check on the work-item dict returned by `wl show` or `wl list`.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` sets `deletedBy` on the work item but **may leave the status untouched** (e.g. `open`, `in_progress`, or `completed`). Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:766`.
- `StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed` and `require_claimed` only check `status` — they do **not** check `deletedBy`. Source: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py:641-730`.
- The downtime dispatcher in ContextHub/herdr filters by `status === 'open'` or `status === 'blocked'` but does **not** filter by `deletedBy`. Source: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:6689, 6740`.
- `implement.py` already correctly skips soft-deleted children via `_is_terminal_child()`, which checks `deletedBy`. Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:761-780`.

## Desired change

Three independent guard points must be hardened:

1. **Worklog CLI**: `wl update --status` (and `wl update` generally) must reject mutations on items with non-empty `deletedBy`.
2. **Shared StatusLifecycle**: `require_claimed` and `ensure_claimed` must check `deletedBy` and refuse to operate on soft-deleted items.
3. **Downtime dispatcher**: the worker must filter out items where `deletedBy` is set, in addition to existing status filters.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `require_claimed`, `ensure_claimed` methods
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reference for `_is_terminal_child` pattern
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — candidate selection and status filters
- Worklog CLI source (dist/cli.js) — `wl update` command implementation

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJ14FQQ006R3PD** — the false-positive test-failure item that was resurrected (deletedBy set, then re-dispatched)
- **SA-0MUTWB8BA003J0V6** — `_is_terminal_child` correctly handles soft-deleted children in implement.py
- **SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9** — claim-invariant: actively worked => in_progress (related to StatusLifecycle design)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Some agents may have already issued `wl update --status` on soft-deleted items before this fix. Mitigation: the fix only prevents future mutations; no rollback needed.
- **Risk:** The downtime dispatcher filters may exist in multiple places (candidate selection, Herdr list grouping, offer computation). All filter paths must be updated.
- **Assumption:** `deletedBy` is always non-empty string when a work item is soft-deleted (never an empty string, whitespace, or null). This is verified by inspecting the `wl delete` implementation.
- **Risk:** Adding checks in StatusLifecycle may break agents that rely on silent re-claim. Mitigation: add tests for each agent workflow that uses `StatusLifecycle`.
- **Scope creep:** This fix does not address why `wl delete` may leave status unchanged — that is a separate hygiene issue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should `wl delete` also set `status=deleted` to prevent resurrection?" — Answer: No. The current convention is that `wl delete` sets `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; status is optional to change. This fix makes `deletedBy` the authoritative gate everywhere, which is cleaner. Source: design decision from this intake.
- Q: "Does `wl delete` always set `deletedBy`?" — Answer: Yes, per the `wl delete` command implementation in the Worklog CLI. Source: code inspection.
- Q: "What about imported work items with `deletedBy` set via `wl import`?" — Answer: The audit_runner already filters these. All three new guard points will catch them uniformly. Source: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10769`.

# Add a tests-deleted-vs-added health metric and actively prune tests that no longer map to behaviour

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis currently reports test *additions* and *rewrites* but makes test *deletions* nearly invisible: whole-file deletions are hidden by the default diff filter, and there is no consolidated "tests added vs tests deleted vs net growth" figure per project or per test area. As a result the suite grows roughly 8:1 (82,381 added vs 9,968 deleted lines in modified test files, from the ContextHub analysis) with no health signal and no documented way to prune tests that no longer map to observable behaviour.

## Users

- **Maintainer of the pi agent infrastructure** — wants an honest, consolidated growth metric (added / deleted / modified / net growth) per project and per test area, in both the human report and JSON, so suite growth is visible at a glance without additional analysis.
- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants a trended growth signal over time (per calendar quarter) so regressions in net test growth are visible.
- **Agent enforcing testing policy** — wants a documented, repeatable workflow to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the report to state, per project and per test area, exactly how many tests were added, deleted, modified, and the net growth, so I can see at a glance whether the suite is growing without bound.
- As a producer, I want the added/deleted/net-growth metric trended per calendar quarter, so regressions in test-suite growth are visible over time.
- As an agent, I want a documented review workflow for pruning tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, so pruning decisions rest on the metric plus explicit criteria rather than anecdote.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The analysis reports, per project and per test area: tests added, tests deleted, tests modified, and net growth, in the human report and JSON.
2. Whole-file test deletions are counted (diff filter includes `D`; rename detection applied so moves are not miscounted as deletions).
3. A documented review workflow describes how to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
4. The growth metric is trended over time **per calendar quarter** (derived from commit dates), so regressions are visible.
5. Tests cover the added/deleted accounting, including files deleted and re-added.
6. The metric is exposed by the reproducible `skill/test-churn` skill rather than as a standalone script.
7. At least one testing/validation criterion: the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the skill README/SKILL.md, and `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md`.

## Constraints

- Must live inside the existing `skill/test-churn` skill (AC6); no new standalone script and no ContextHub-specific paths.
- The metric must be derived deterministically from git history via the existing analyser entry point (`skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`), which is read-only against the analysed repository.
- Changes must not regress the corrected methodology implemented under `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW` (real git name-status, documented rewrite-ratio denominators, distinct-commit temporal rates, whole-file deletion accounting).
- Growth trend granularity is calendar quarter derived from commit dates (operator decision Q2); release/tag-based grouping is out of scope.
- The item delivers metric + documented workflow only; the actual pruning pass is a follow-on item, not part of this work (operator decision Q3).
- Work item descriptions/comments in Markdown, UK English.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` already computes: `modified_test_deletions`, `modified_test_additions`, `new_test_file_additions`, `deleted_test_files`, `deleted_test_lines`, and per-area `new_files` / `deleted_files` / `total_added` / `total_deleted` / `rewrites`.
- Whole-file deletion accounting exists (spans whole history, including test-only commits) and `--diff-filter=ADMRT` already includes `D`; AC2 is *mostly* satisfied but lacks explicit tests for delete-and-re-add.
- The temporal trend (`analyse_temporal_trends`) is currently **monthly rewrite-rate** only — there is no quarterly net-growth trend (AC4 is new work).
- No consolidated net-growth figure and no documented pruning workflow exist (AC1 headline and AC3 are new work).
- The skill's tests (`skill/test-churn/tests/`) cover deletion accounting in test-only commits and rename detection, but not file deleted and re-added (AC5 gap).

## Problem Statement

Once session logs are parsed, the skill must extract repeated confusion patterns using deterministic heuristics — tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals, tool result errors, and retry/self-correction patterns. Raw logs are too large and noisy to send to an LLM directly.

## Goal

As a skill author, I want deterministic heuristic extraction of confusion signals from parsed sessions — counts, distributions, and capped excerpts — so the LLM classification stage receives compact, distilled input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tool call distribution: counts of each tool name across the 20 sessions, with per-tool error rates.
- [ ] Thinking-content error signals: detect keywords (`error`, `fail`, `retry`, `incorrect`, `sorry`, `wrong`, `fix`, `correct`, `issue`, `problem`, `confused`, `wait`, `actually`, `oh`, `hmm`, `ah`) in thinking content, with a context window around each hit.
- [ ] Tool result errors: detect tracebacks, `permission denied`, `command not found`, and shell expansion errors in `toolResult` content where `isError == true` or content text matches error patterns.
- [ ] Retry/self-correction patterns: detect repeated tool calls with identical arguments within a session, and detect sequences of (tool call → error result → modified tool call).
- [ ] False-positive mitigation: keyword matches are context-windowed; known legitimate uses (e.g. "error handling" in code text) are classified with surrounding context so the LLM can confirm.
- [ ] Per-session excerpt size is capped (configurable, default e.g. 2 KB/session) to bound the LLM prompt.
- [ ] Unit tests cover each signal type with synthetic session fixtures, including at least one borderline false-positive case.
- [ ] A `--max-sessions` and `--errors-only` CLI flag are exposed (or documented as function arguments) for deterministic testing.

## Constraints

- Deterministic and side-effect free: no LLM calls, no file writes.
- Configurable keyword lists (module-level constants) so tests and future tuning are easy.
- Excerpts must never exceed the configured cap.

## Key Files

- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — heuristic extraction functions (`extract_tool_distribution`, `extract_thinking_signals`, `extract_tool_errors`, `extract_retry_patterns`)
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — heuristic unit tests

## Dependencies

- Feature 1 (session log parser) — must be complete first.

## Problem Statement

Heuristic signals are useful but noisy. The skill needs LLM-assisted interpretation to classify patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generate actionable recommendations — without sending raw multi-megabyte logs to the model.

## Goal

As a skill author, I want an LLM classification stage that sends only distilled heuristic signals (counts + capped excerpts) to a non-interactive `pi` call and receives structured pattern categories plus recommendations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Invokes `pi -p --print` (non-interactive mode) following the audit skill's `_call_pi()` pattern for subprocess LLM calls.
- [ ] Prompt contains only distilled signals (counts, distributions, capped excerpts) — never raw session log content.
- [ ] Requested output is structured JSON (via prompt instruction) with fields: `categories` (list of `{name, confidence, evidence_sessions, summary}`) and `recommendations` (list of `{title, issue_type, target_skill, rationale, evidence_sessions}`).
- [ ] Response parsing is fail-soft: malformed JSON from the model degrades to a diagnostic error rather than a crash.
- [ ] Session IDs of the analysed sessions are included in the prompt so evidence citations map back.
- [ ] Integration test uses a mocked `pi` subprocess (injected via a callable or subprocess runner) to assert: (a) the prompt excludes raw log content, (b) prompt size stays under a documented budget (e.g. 32 KB), (c) a well-formed model response parses into categories and recommendations, (d) a malformed response is handled without raising.
- [ ] No secrets are sent: heuristic excerpts pass through the same redaction used by the report (see Feature 4).

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics do extraction, LLM does classification — never LLM-only.
- Single LLM call per run (cost control): all signals batched into one prompt.
- Whisper: no tools enabled for the classification call (`--no-tools` or equivalent) so the model returns text only; follow the audit skill's context-reduction flags where applicable.
- Model selection configurable (default to the project's local proxy model), with a `--model` flag.

## Key Files

- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — `classify_patterns(signals, model=..., runner=...)` function and `_call_pi(prompt, model)` helper
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — mocked-pi classification tests

The skill must present its findings as a structured report in the agent response — summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations — in a deterministic, machine-readable form.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a deterministic report rendered to stdout (Markdown) with an optional `--json` mode for machine consumption, so I can review and cite the analysis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Report has a clear summary section: number of sessions analysed, date range, sessions skipped (fail-soft counters).
- [ ] Top patterns section: sorted by frequency (descending) then alphabetically (deterministic ordering), each with count and evidence session citations.
- [ ] Recommended improvements section: each recommendation with rationale and evidence citations listing which sessions showed which pattern.
- [ ] Evidence citations use session file names, not full paths, and reference specific pattern occurrences (e.g. "sessions: a.jsonl, b.jsonl").
- [ ] `--json` flag emits the full report as a single JSON document (structured, machine-readable).
- [ ] Human-readable (default) mode emits Markdown with all required sections.
- [ ] Output is deterministic for the same input directory: sorting is explicit everywhere.
- [ ] Secrets redaction is applied to all output (paths matching `.ssh`/`.env`, API key patterns like `sk-...`, `Bearer ...`) before rendering.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) report rendering with required sections, (b) deterministic ordering, (c) `--json` structure, (d) redaction of secret-like strings.

Per the parent work item's acceptance criteria, actionable recommendations must be filed as worklog comments on the parent item, and each recommendation must auto-create a child work item (issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description). This is the automation that closes the loop between analysis and skill improvement.

## Goal

As an operator, I want the skill to file recommendations as worklog comments and auto-create child work items (without implementing them), so improvement suggestions are tracked and prioritised downstream.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a successful analysis, the skill files the report's recommendations as a worklog comment on the parent work item (the item from which the skill was invoked, i.e. CWD project's parent if determinable else an explicit `--parent-id` argument).
- [ ] For each recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature` (chosen per recommendation), priority `low` or `medium`, assigned to `Map`.
- [ ] Each created child's description links back via `related-to:<parent-id>` so traceability is bidirectional.
- [ ] Idempotence: re-running the skill on the same recommendations does not create duplicate child items — same-title items are reused (matched by title), and a reference to the existing item is recorded instead.
- [ ] The parent work item's ACs do NOT get implemented here — work-item creation only, no code changes.
- [ ] A dry-run flag (`--dry-run`) prints what would be created without mutating the worklog.
- [ ] Unit tests (mocked `wl` runner) cover: (a) comment filing, (b) child creation with correct issue-type/assignee/linking, (c) idempotent re-run, (d) dry-run performs no mutations.

- Use `wl` commands via the worklog-safe runner (worktree-aware) exactly as the rest of the tooling does.
